defects.title: ac_plugin.search_hooks() hardcodes a steering opinion instead of reading caller-set module state, so --plugin partura.ac_plugin silently steers every AlphaCube run and cannot be turned off
defects.failure_scenario: Design step 3 and the design's own code sample specify `search_hooks()` as "a SearchHooks built from module state the caller sets" (the same pattern as set_scorer_state), read by "cli / idea_search". The implementation takes no state: it always returns SearchHooks(op_weight=<0.0 for every resource_risk spec not in ops_ext.NEW_OPERATORS>), and cli.py:157 does `hooks = search_hooks_from(_plugin_names(a))` unconditionally for --plugin AND $ALPHACUBE_PLUGINS. Measured against the live registry (/Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP11/attack_search_hooks.py): (a) with `--allow-resource-risk`, 281 searchable specs and exactly 4 of them -- in_mask_nearby_ones, nt_ts_pearson, nt_ts_spearman, pow -- are forced to weight 0, i.e. the flag the user passed to enable them is silently cancelled for those four, with no opt-out; (b) with the CLI default allow_resource_risk=False there are 277 specs and ZERO get weight 0, so the hook changes no weight at all -- yet because `op_weight is not None` routes _pick into _pick_weighted (random.choices instead of random.choice), `TypedTreeGenerator(reg, seed=7, op_weight=hooks.op_weight).generate_population(30)` differs from `TypedTreeGenerator(reg, seed=7)` at index 0. So `alphacube mine --plugin partura.ac_plugin --fitness rank_ic --seed 7`, run only to get Partura's 45 operators, is not comparable to the same command without --plugin. The function's own docstring claims it "leave[s] sampling and acceptance otherwise exactly as today", which is false. Separately, scripts/idea_search.py never calls it, so the base_weight formula now exists twice (ac_plugin.py:195 and idea_search.py:152) and can drift.
defects.suggested_fix: Add module state as the design asks (e.g. `_hooks: Optional[SearchHooks] = None` plus `set_search_hooks(...)`) and have `search_hooks()` return `_hooks if _hooks is not None else SearchHooks()` -- i.e. NO opinion by default, so loading the plugin for its operators leaves the generator byte-identical. Then have scripts/idea_search.py set that state and build both arms' hooks through `ac_plugin.search_hooks()` so there is one copy of base_weight. If the resource-risk down-weighting is genuinely wanted as a default, it must at minimum be documented as a behaviour change on the CLI path and be switchable (e.g. a `PARTURA_AC_PLUGIN_HOOKS=off` / explicit setter), and the docstring's "sampling ... exactly as today" claim removed.

defects.title: Nothing pins which arm gets the guidance and the idea boost: swapping the control/steer hooks leaves all 48 tests green
defects.failure_scenario: Verified empirically: I exported the commit to a scratch copy, replaced idea_search.py:192 with `HOOKS = {"control": SearchHooks(op_weight=weighted, accept=guidance_accept), "steer": SearchHooks(op_weight=base_weight)}` (control gets the boost AND the guidance, steer gets neither) and ran the suite in the copy -- 18 passed, i.e. the whole test file stays green with the single scientific claim of the script inverted. `test_search_hooks_for_control_and_steer_differ_only_in_op_weight_and_accept` cannot catch it because it does not use the script's hooks at all: it builds `control = SearchHooks(op_weight=lambda s: 1.0)` and `steer = SearchHooks(op_weight=lambda s: 1.0, accept=steer_accept)`, i.e. two hand-made hooks with IDENTICAL op_weight, and then asserts `pop_c == pop_s` -- a statement about the generator, not about the arms its name claims to compare. The only other check on the arms is the string grep at tests/test_ac_plugin.py:316, `'HOOKS = {"control":' in src or "HOOKS[arm]" in src`, whose `or` branch is satisfied by `HOOKS[arm]` alone. Same gap for base_weight/weighted themselves: dropping the BOOST factor from `weighted` is also untested.
defects.suggested_fix: Make the arm construction importable and test it directly instead of grepping: move `base_weight` / `weighted` / `HOOKS` out of scripts/idea_search.py's `with slot():` body into a small pure helper (e.g. `ac_plugin.arm_hooks(arm, *, risky, ext, opw, idea_ops, boost, accept)`), then assert on it -- control's op_weight(spec of an IDEA_OP) == 1.0 while steer's == BOOST, control.accept is None while steer.accept is the guidance, and all other SearchHooks fields equal. Build a real TypedTreeGenerator from each with allow_resource_risk=True and assert the idea operator appears strictly more often under the steer hooks, so the design's test bullet ("a generator built from each yields the expected populations") is actually exercised.

defects.title: The guidance's thinning stream is random.Random(SEED) with SEED == the miner's own seed -- the exact collision AlphaCube's _hook_seed was written to avoid
defects.failure_scenario: idea_search.py passes `seed=SEED` to run_mining, so GPMiner does `self._rng = random.Random(SEED)` and hands that object to TypedTreeGenerator as `rng=`. The script then seeds its own thinning stream with the same value: `hook_rng = random.Random(SEED)` (lines 154 and 215). mining/generator.py's `_hook_seed` docstring states exactly this case as the reason it derives hook_rng from the generator stream's `getstate()` rather than from `seed`: "at seed=0 that stream is byte-for-byte self._rng itself, so a hook thinning on hook_rng.random() would be reading the generator's own draws." With the default `--seed 0` the guidance's u-values are therefore the same sequence the tree builder draws from (a separate object, so the tree stream is not disturbed and the run IS reproducible from the seed -- which is why this is low -- but the independence WP5 engineered for is given up).
defects.suggested_fix: Seed the script's stream off a namespaced string instead of the bare miner seed, which random.Random hashes with SHA-512 and is stable across runs/platforms: `hook_rng = random.Random(f"partura.idea_search/{SEED}/{arm}")`. Per-arm namespacing also removes the (harmless today) fact that both arms share one u-sequence.

defects.title: The view_id change orphans the entire shared panel cache, while the code comment and the test that names the claim both say it is a no-op for existing entries
defects.failure_scenario: partura/panels.py:222 appends `|{self.store.contract_hash}` to the raw string that is sha1'd into view_id, and panels.py:229 keys every on-disk panel as `sha1(view_id|expr_key)`. So every cache entry written before WP11 -- including the `__label__|...` target entries -- becomes unreachable on the first run after this lands, and nothing in panels.py ever deletes orphans (no unlink/rmtree anywhere in the file), so `runs/_panels` keeps the dead files and the next run recomputes every panel. The comment at panels.py:216-221 says "this is a no-op for every existing cache entry" and the test at tests/test_ac_plugin.py:278, `test_view_id_matches_contract_hash_byte_identical_claim_with_no_daily_source`, claims in its own docstring that "view_id's new term is a no-op for every cache entry written before WP11" -- but it only asserts `CubeStore(dir).contract_hash == store.contract_hash`, never that view_id is unchanged, which it cannot be. The invalidation itself is what design step 9 asked for; the false claim is what will mislead whoever budgets the next server run.
defects.suggested_fix: Reword the comment and the test's docstring to say what actually happens -- the daily-aware contract_hash is byte-identical for a store with no daily source, but view_id moves for every entry, so the shared panel cache is invalidated once by this change. Rename the test to what it asserts (e.g. test_contract_hash_is_unchanged_without_a_daily_source), and either add a one-off orphan sweep in PanelSet (delete cache files not matching the current view_id prefix) or note the manual `rm -rf runs/_panels` in the migration notes.

defects.title: Design step 8 (unaccepted_fallbacks per arm in evidence.json) is unimplemented, and the steer arm's fallback path is now much wider than before
defects.failure_scenario: The deviation is correctly diagnosed -- `miner_ref` is a local at pipeline.py:307 and RunResult carries no miner/generator, so the caller genuinely cannot reach `TypedTreeGenerator.unaccepted_fallbacks`. But the consequence is worse after WP11 than before it: with `accept` set, generator.py:271 raises generate()'s fallback budget from `tries=1` to GENERATE_FALLBACK_TRIES=64 and, on exhaustion, returns an un-accepted `relaxed` tree while incrementing `unaccepted_fallbacks`. So the steer arm can now be fed a population the guidance never approved, in a quantity nothing reports, and the steer/control read-out in evidence.json has no way to show it -- exactly the confound the design wanted measured. Reproducible: my end-to-end run at /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP11/attack_e2e.py shows the steer arm thinning 25 of 60 proposals with no counter for how many slots were then filled by an unaccepted fallback.
defects.suggested_fix: Out of WP11's file list, so leave the code as is, but hand the next AlphaCube package a concrete ask: add `unaccepted_fallbacks` (and `generations`/`stopped_early` alongside) to `RunResult` in src/alphacube/pipeline.py, filled from `miner_ref[0].generator.unaccepted_fallbacks` after `m.mine(...)` at pipeline.py:390 -- one field and one assignment -- then have idea_search.py read `res.unaccepted_fallbacks` into evidence["arms"][arm] and replace the comment at idea_search.py:247-252.

result.notes:
Suite: 48 passed, 3 warnings in 4.98s (Partura-steering, tests/). The commit touches no AlphaCube file and both worktrees are clean (`git status --porcelain` empty in each), so AlphaCube's 617/10/1 baseline is untouched.

Files touched: exactly partura/ac_plugin.py, partura/ops_ext.py, partura/panels.py, scripts/idea_search.py, tests/test_ac_plugin.py -- the four owned files plus the test module. Nothing outside the list.

What I verified as CORRECT, by running it rather than reading it (scripts left in /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura/tmp/impl/review_WP11/, nothing committed, no tracked file touched):

- probe_flags.py: against an unpatched build_registry with ops_ext imported, the registry is 304 entries and ZERO of the nine declared kernels is boolean_output/trivial_boolean. Clearing `real_valued` back to False in OPERATOR_REGISTRY and rebuilding flags exactly 11 entries -- the 9 base names plus nt_cs_bucket_demean / nt_cs_bucket_zscore -- so the design's "11 entries / 9 base names" is right, the test is real (it goes red if the flag is removed), and the nt_ twin propagation works. Crucially, NO OTHER entry among the 45 NEW_OPERATORS (90 entries with twins) is flagged, so dropping the old blanket `dataclasses.replace` clear over all 45 costs nothing: there is no silent vocabulary regression. searchable(include_boolean=False, include_resource_risk=True) goes 278 -> 281 after register(), i.e. the declare_real_valued(in_sustain_*) line moves it by exactly the +3 the design claims.
- attack_warmup.py: the warmup>0 path, which the implementer only reasoned about. With a synthetic store, start=dates[60], warmup=20 -> trim=20, `make_scorer(target_full, "partura", dates=list(view.dates), warmup=trim)` gives _warmup=20 and _cut=40 (= the cut computed on the trimmed axis), and `score(full_panel)["fit"]` is bit-equal to `0.03 * steer_reward(panel[trim:], ctx, kind)["score"]` (0.04095688911166666 both sides). The misalignment guard also fires correctly when ctx is built WITHOUT the trim: "the GP's label grid (80, 40) ... is not Partura's (100, 40)". So the design's must_fix #6 (the trim hazard that used to kill an arm silently once --start moved) is genuinely closed, not just documented.
- attack_e2e.py: two arms through the real run_mining -> GPMiner -> TypedTreeGenerator with trim=20 and `gp_params={... 'hooks': ...}`. Both arms complete, the scorer is constructed once per arm with _warmup=20/_cut=40, the steer arm's counters populate ({'proposed': 60, 'accepted': 35, 'thinned': 25}) and the control arm's stay empty -- so the hooks really do route through gp_params and the arms differ only in the intervention.
- attack_fullcatalog.py: install_kernels() no longer running at import is NOT a parse regression. default_full_catalog() builds from OPERATOR_REGISTRY (fullcatalog.py's own docstring: "Entries come from (1) every @op-decorated function"), not from operator_dict_DT/_ND, so all 45 kernels are in it (335 entries) with or without install_kernels(), and parse_research over all 1465 expression strings in the repo's YAML gives the identical ok/fail split (487/978) both ways. Nothing in src/alphacube reads operator_dict_DT/_ND, so that table is only for external legacy callers now.
- Default-parameter / RNG neutrality of the new branches: _pick_weighted's face mass is `sum(w)/len(kept)` over SURVIVING operators, which is exactly the old script's `pick` (positive-weight denominator, design must_fix #3), so the control arm reproduces the pre-migration control arm; `accept=None` on the control arm keeps generate()'s fallback at tries=1 (generator.py:271), i.e. byte-identical to pre-WP5; mutation_checks_bans defaults True for both arms, so the arms do NOT differ in whether the mutate_window/mutate_constant ban hole is open (design must_fix #4 satisfied); ban_top_n=0/rolling_block=0 means banned_substructures is empty for both.
- ctx.base IS the old script's known_z (RewardContext(..., base=known_z) at idea_search.py:115), so replacing `k = known_z[:cut:5]` with `_ctx.base[:self._cut:5]` is numerically identical; min_coverage=0.9 still reaches PanelScorer through **kw exactly as the old monkeypatched make_scorer delivered it; GPMiner's `_target_t64`/`_target_ranks_t` are assigned at gp.py:349-350 and read nowhere else in the tree, so the scorer handing back the TRIMMED tensors cannot misalign anything.
- The deviations about design steps 7 and 8 are factually right: miner_ref is a local (pipeline.py:307), run_mining's signature has no miner/callback parameter that leaks the GPMiner, RunResult has no such field, and SearchHooks.accept is checked by `inspect.signature(accept).bind(object())` (generator.py:102) so a hook cannot take a generator argument.
- tests/test_ac_plugin.py's grep test currently passes against the real /Users/wxy/Desktop/Partura tree too: the only files anywhere under it carrying the six needles are the pre-WP11 scripts/idea_search.py and partura/ops_ext.py, which this commit replaces -- so merging ac-plugin into the main checkout will not turn that test red. It will, however, go red on any future scratch .py left under the worktree (it rglobs the whole tree and only excludes /.git/ and itself) or on a legitimate future `from alphacube.mining.scoring import FITNESS_KINDS`; worth knowing, not worth fixing now.

Untested but verified correct by hand: the factory's `cut` on the warmup>0 axis (no test covers warmup>0 for the cut; my attack_warmup.py does), and `len(dates) != target.shape[0]` is not validated by the factory (GPMiner always keeps them consistent, so this is latent only).

Not defects, for the record: not passing leaf_slots/daily_fields to the steer arm (design step 6 lists them, but run_mining is called without daily_root, so daily leaves would be unevaluable and silently dropped -- omitting them is the right call); deleting the whole inline ParturaScorer block rather than only the lines the design names (it would be dead duplicate code); the removal of ops_ext's `catalog._DEFAULT = None` reset (the design's own judge says "drop Partura's catalog._DEFAULT = None reset either way", and bridge.ensure_alphacube_on_path is what puts alphacube on sys.path, so the registry cannot be built before ops_ext is imported in any Partura entry point); `steer_reward` now being an unused import in scripts/idea_search.py (lint only); `--arms foo` now raising KeyError instead of silently running a control-like arm (fail-loud is better). The Co-Authored-By line says "Claude Sonnet 5" rather than the "Claude Opus 5.5" the computed task asked for -- flagged by the implementer and left for the orchestrator; I did not amend it.
